ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening of all general partner officers, limited partners and qualifying UBOs against: (i) Global Affairs Canada consolidated autonomous sanctions instruments under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (ii) United Nations Security Council consolidated lists enforced under the United Nations Act; (iii) Public Safety Canada and RCMP domestic terrorist entity listings under Criminal Code s. 83.05 regulations; and (iv) the U.S. OFAC SDN list and BIS Denied Persons screening, given USD-denominated app-store rails and U.S. distribution counterparties. Politically exposed person (PEP) determination follows the FINTRAC policy framework: foreign PEPs are subject to mandatory predictive screening, and domestic PEPs are matched against a public officials database and flagged as higher risk. Continuous transaction monitoring and a five-year record retention standard consistent with PCMLTFA record-keeping requirements apply. FINTRAC money services business registration is not triggered where Apple IAP and Google Play Billing act as merchant of record and the limited partnership does not handle cash or payment directly; a stand-by registration reservation is nevertheless documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and the NUANS Name Search System operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), with name booking and limited partnership registration completed through the applicable provincial registry portal (e.g., ServiceOntario), which accepts the NUANS preliminary report as the mandatory name-clearance output
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names must be available in both English and French under the Official Languages Act R.S.C. 1985, c. 31 (4th Supp.); Latin-script names require no statutory transliteration, and registries accept bilingual legal names with a French form recorded in the charter documents. For extra-provincial registration in Quebec, the Charter of the French Language (arts. 63 to 68, CQLR c. C-11) requires the French version of the name to be given precedence and to appear in all registration filings. Where a proposed name originates in a non-Latin alphabet script, the registry mandates a Romanized transliteration on the NUANS report and in the documents of record; the foreign-script brand may be used only as an operating trading name and not as the registered legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: any word implying federal or provincial sponsorship, a government connection, or a regulated professional license where no such license is held
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant receives a written refusal decision or refusal code from Corporations Canada or the provincial registry within five business days of filing. The applicant may immediately re-file up to two perfected alternate NUANS reports without penalty. A formal administrative review is available under s. 25 of the Canada Business Corporations Act, directed to the Director, within a 30-day window; the applicant must file a written submission, the original refusal notice, a legal interpretive memorandum on any conflicting mark, and evidence of third-party consent or registered-user consent. For a limited partnership, the equivalent provincial appeal lies to the provincial registrar within 15 days of refusal, supported by a rebuttal addressing confusing similarity under s. 12 of the Trademarks Act R.S.C. 1985, c. T-13. If all appeal avenues are exhausted, the applicant may adopt a numbered limited partnership name and thereafter request an extra-provincial license carrying the operating name as a trading style.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an ISIC 6201 digital health app limited partnership. Every Canadian province requires a real registered office address for service of process within the jurisdiction; a licensed registered agent office offering mail-forwarding, scan-and-forward and business access hours is accepted by most registrars and is standard for app-based pass-through vehicles. The Canada Revenue Agency expects books and records to be reasonably accessible at or through that address, but no industry-specific requirement for a physical server, clinic or laboratory exists for a fitness telemetry app operating through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing. Quebec, however, applies a stricter rule for extra-provincially registered enterprises, requiring a physical place of business in Quebec for valid service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Annualized unannounced physical inspection risk is approximately 5-10% for a low-risk digital health limited partnership. The principal triggers are an anomalous T5013 partnership filing, a GST/HST registration mismatch, or a Canada Revenue Agency books-and-records request. FINTRAC on-site compliance examinations occur only if the entity becomes a reporting entity or is suspected of exemption abuse. RCMP or integrated financial enforcement teams may attend the registered office only under judicial warrant in an active sanctions investigation; the quantified probability for a standard fitness tracker merchant-of-record model is estimated at under 7%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, ss. 2, 3, 5 and 10 (provincial LP statute; federal CBCA does not govern limited partnerships), read with Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44 for any corporate general partner
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (Ontario: ServiceOntario Companies and Partnerships Portal; other provinces maintain equivalent registries)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form 1 under the Limited Partnerships Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the general and limited partners agree capital contributions solely by the partnership agreement, and any escrow of contributions is contractual, not statutory
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The initial General Partner and the initial Limited Partner of [LP Name] are admitted upon execution of the partnership agreement; (2) the registered office shall be [address], Ontario, and the initial registered agent is appointed; (3) the partnership agreement is ratified; (4) the General Partner is authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the provincial registry and the initial capital contribution may be held in escrow pending issuance of the certificate; (5) the General Partner is appointed governing officer to open bank accounts, obtain tax accounts, and maintain statutory records; (6) all filings and incidental acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) via NUANS; provincial registry of partnerships
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed limited partnership name; ensure the name contains a permitted limited partnership designation (e.g., 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP'); file the name reservation or receive the search report before drafting the declaration. Provide notarized consent of any partner whose personal name is used in the firm name.
required_dossiers: Proposed LP name containing 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP'
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is confusingly similar to an existing mark, submit a revised NUANS search with a distinct secondary element, or appeal to ISED Name Decision Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Declaration and Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed paralegal or attorney; notarization by a notary public in the registering province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form 1) and the operating partnership agreement. Execute the declaration before a witness or notary; have each general partner sign the declaration and each limited partner execute the agreement. Note that only general partners possess management authority.
required_dossiers: Identification and address of each general and limited partner
Consent to act as registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries a defect in the declaration, file an amended declaration correcting the defect within 15 days; late correction may require a court application for rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Declaration with Provincial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (ServiceOntario portal or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership online or in-person to the provincial registry and pay the prescribed filing fee. The registry will issue the Certificate of Limited Partnership upon approval. No LSD registration is required because the entity is a pass-through partnership.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incomplete particulars, file an amended declaration or objection with the registry; a legal review under the Partnerships Act may be used to cure rejection within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Canadian Business Bank Account and Registering Federal Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I chartered bank or credit union; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business bank account in the LP name using the Certificate of Limited Partnership and partnership agreement; register the LP with the CRA for a Business Number (BN), GST/HST account, and payroll account (if employees are hired). The vulnerable-sector clearance is not a condition precedent to formation.
required_dossiers: CRA Form RC1 signed by an authorized general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account opening is delayed due to KYC queries, provide notarized partnership records and obtain a CRA-registered business number; escalation to the bank compliance team cures most administrative holds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Compliance: Registered Office, Records, and Annual Returns
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial registrar; CRA; municipal business licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain a registered office address in the province of formation; keep the register of partners, partnership agreement, and financial books; file the provincial annual return where applicable and the T5013 partnership information return with the CRA annually.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence (if office is operated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the partnership misses an annual filing, file a late return with the provincial registry and pay the reinstatement fee; CRA late-filing penalties may be waived under taxpayer relief provisions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the business is a pure digital health application service with no manufacturing or physical production facility
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required under federal or provincial industrial licensing; municipal general business licence may apply to the office location

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / provincial environmental ministry
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software development and cloud-based telemetry services have no physical project footprints; no EIA registration or report required unless the business later establishes owned data centers or hardware assembly
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero wastewater or VOC discharge from any industrial process; compliance with Canada's E-waste Regulations for any discarded electronic hardware; digital services must meet accessibility standards but no environmental discharge thresholds apply

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or workplace clearance is required for a virtual app business. If a physical office is leased, the tenant must obtain a municipal occupancy permit and post-fire-safety plan; no occupational clearance under provincial health and safety statutes applies beyond general WHMIS and first-aid requirements for any employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), the federal tax authority administering income tax, GST/HST, and related statutes; primary portal is CRA My Account at canada.ca/cra
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian Limited Partnerships obtain a Business Number (BN) upon formation through the CRA online BN application or by submitting Form RC59; foreign-owned entities register as non-residents if carrying on business in Canada; GST/HST registration is triggered separately upon meeting turnover thresholds
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Limited Partnerships are statutorily classified as pass-through entities under the Income Tax Act with no entity-level taxation; no federal check-the-box election exists, though hybrid mismatch and GAAR provisions may apply in cross-border structures

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD annual gross revenue threshold triggering mandatory GST/HST registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: CRA-mandated issuance of compliant tax invoices; electronic filing of GST/HST returns via My Business Account is statutory; real-time fiscal clearance and API stamping not required for standard registrants but mandatory for large-volume filers under modernization rules

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST rate applies to exports of goods and offshore services where the supply is deemed to occur outside Canada, with the recipient being a non-resident and proof of export provided
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in full tax assessment, interest charges, penalties up to 200% of evaded amount, and potential criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - monetary authority and issuer of legal tender. Canada maintains no separate foreign-exchange control ministry or exchange-control statute. Foreign-exchange transaction surveillance is discharged by FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; prudential supervision of banks and the clearing system resides with OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) and Payments Canada; inward foreign investment screening is administered by ISED (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) under the Investment Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has full current- and capital-account convertibility (IMF Article VIII status) and operates a freely floating CAD. No exchange-control approval, currency conversion licence, quota, or surrender obligation applies to inbound capital contributions, outbound trade settlements, partnership allocations, or profit repatriation of a Canadian Limited Partnership. Remittance hurdles are exclusively tax-driven: the CA_LP files a T5013 partnership information return and allocates income to partners; non-resident partners are taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act on Canadian-source business income and, unless they file a Canadian tax return, the partnership must withhold Part XIII tax at 25% on income allocations paid or credited (treaty relief to 5-15%, or elimination for business profits not attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment). Capital distributions are non-taxable and freely remittable. GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters; for app sales through Apple/Google, the platform operators are generally responsible for collecting GST/HST on Canadian consumer purchases, requiring the LP treasury to reconcile net-of-tax platform remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory repatriation timeline: none. Mandatory conversion ratio into CAD: 0%. The Income Tax Act and Currency Act impose no forced conversion, retention period, or surrender of export proceeds. Export revenue may lawfully be held in USD or any foreign currency at a Canadian Schedule I bank or foreign bank account. Practical constraints: (i) FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reports apply to incoming and outgoing transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, with foreign-origin incoming wires reported by the Canadian receiving financial institution; (ii) foreign-currency revenue must be translated into CAD at the Bank of Canada noon exchange rate (or a CRA-designated rate) for each taxation year under subsection 261(2) of the Income Tax Act; (iii) foreign bank accounts of partners aggregating above CAD 100,000 must be reported on Form T1135.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM. Foreign digital EMIs and banking-as-a-service providers (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, Mercury, Brex) may serve as secondary multi-currency collection accounts for USD/EUR/GBP Apple/Google payouts, but they are not 'banks' under the Bank Act (Canada), are not CDIC members, and deposits held with them are uninsured. A foreign EMI holding deposits for Canadian residents may constitute unauthorized deposit-taking unless it operates as an authorized foreign bank or a FINTRAC-registered money services business. Recommended architecture: Schedule I domestic accounts as the primary treasury anchor; one curated fintech EMI as a low-cost USD/EUR collection accelerator with daily zero-balance sweeps to the domestic operating account. EMI onboarding of a Canadian LP with non-resident partners is frequently declined absent a Canadian registered agent and a fully documented UBO chain.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permissible as a matter of federal law. FINTRAC identity-ascertainment guidance allows authorized signatories of a limited partnership to be identified remotely by: (i) a government-issued photo document verified via live video; (ii) a Canadian credit-file match; or (iii) attestation by a responsible person (lawyer or notary). The bank will require: a certified copy of the LP's registration certificate, the full limited partnership agreement, a general-partner resolution adopting the account mandate, and personal KYC for all general partners and signatories. In-branch or enhanced interview may be mandated where: (a) the general partner is non-resident or a foreign corporation; (b) any beneficial owner resides in a high-risk or sanctions-hit jurisdiction; or (c) the registered office is not the physical place of business. No statutory in-person mandate exists for a Canadian-registered LP with a resident general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner control: the CA_LP permits non-resident ownership; a UBO holding through a low-tax or opaque intermediate entity triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth inquiry, and possibly negative-media review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organization chart; certified passports and proof of address for every 25%+ partner; tax residence certificates (Canadian Form RC1415 or foreign equivalents); two years of audited financial statements or a bank reference for each material partner; sworn source-of-funds declaration for the proposed capital contribution; engagement letter of the Canadian registered agent confirming LP maintenance; written explanation of the legitimate business rationale for the Canadian LP structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border digital platform receipts: recurring EFTs from Apple Inc. (US) or Google LLC (US) without matching supplier contracts generate FINTRAC EFT reports (threshold CAD 10,000) and 'unexpected large credit' alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement; weekly/monthly platform payout statements mapped to the bank ledger; app-store financial reports; a standing reconciliation workbook; specimen commercial invoices; and a written narrative of the gross-to-net commission waterfall.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume low-value microtransactions from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing may be algorithmically misclassified as structuring or unlicensed money-service activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML risk-tier assessment confirming Low_Risk_Standard (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 digital health app); reasoned legal memorandum demonstrating the LP is not an MSB because it performs no third-party funds transfer or value storage; product architecture documents showing read-only biometric tracking and no payments intermediary function; merchant agreements; monthly transaction volume and average-ticket dashboard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty-name mismatch: Apple/Google pay a developer under a trade name or a US parent entity while the receiving bank account is styled to the CA_LP, triggering beneficiary-verification friction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assignment or settlement-direction agreement between the US parent/general partner and the CA_LP; bank beneficiary confirmation letter; T5013 partnership allocation schedule; certificate of good standing from the LP registry; corporate authorization resolutions from both entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of source of funds for a large inbound capital injection from a foreign related corporation could trigger a Suspicious Transaction Report obligation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolutions of the contributing partner; audited financial statements evidencing retained earnings; executed intercompany capital-contribution agreement; SWIFT MT103 remittance instruction citing purpose code 'COMC'; legal opinion addressing Investment Canada Act notification (Form IP) and confirming the contribution is not derived from proceeds of crime.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) execute a capital-contribution resolution of the general partner and an officer's certificate of the contributing partner; (2) instruct an SWIFT MT103 (gpi) wire from the partner's foreign bank to the CA_LP's CAD account at a Canadian Schedule I bank, using the LP's exact registered legal name and domestic bank/branch number; (3) populate Field 70 (Remittance Information) with 'INITIAL CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - [partner name] - [LP agreement date]'; (4) use ISO 20022 Purpose Code 'COMC' (commercial payment) or 'INTC' (intra-group transfer) where the contributor is the parent; (5) include complete ordering-party identity and address in Field 50K to satisfy FATF Recommendation 16 and FINTRAC EFT reporting. The receiving bank reports incoming EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more and will hold funds in a segregated Capital Escrow Account until KYC is fully satisfied. Investment Canada Act: establishment of a new Canadian business by a non-Canadian requires only a post-closing Form IP notice to ISED within 30 days (no pre-merger review for new businesses); the WTO acquisition-of-control enterprise-value review threshold (approximately CAD 1.3-1.4 billion in 2025) is irrelevant at this capital scale; a national-security review under section 25.3 of the ICA is theoretically available for health-data technologies, so the defense file should evidence de-identified data architecture, Canadian data-residency commitments, and absence of connected-supplier risk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 (gpi) for foreign vendor and contractor payments, citing the commercial invoice in Field 70 with full beneficiary account detail; (ii) domestic CAD low-value recurring payments via ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System) ACH; (iii) same-day large-value CAD wires via Lynx RTGS (the LVTS successor) operated by Payments Canada; (iv) USD clearing within North America via the Canadian bank's US correspondent over Fedwire or CHIPS; (v) commercial letters of credit are permissible at Schedule I banks but commercially unnecessary for digital-services trade - documentary collection against invoice is the market standard; (vi) Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settle on net terms via ACH (US) or SEPA (EU) credit to the designated developer account, requiring monthly gross-to-net reconciliation of platform commission (15-30%), platform-collected taxes, and chargebacks. Recommended treasury structure: zero-balance disbursement sub-account, pre-funded threshold, and automated CAD/USD sweep from the settlement ledger to the tax and reserve accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX deliverable plain-vanilla forwards (CAD/USD) with tenors up to 12 months, documented under a Canadian Bankers Association FX master agreement or ISDA 2002; no mandatory clearing for end-users below OSFI non-cleared derivative margin thresholds
Window forwards (scheduled monthly CAD/USD settlements) aligned to Apple/Google weekly settlement cycles
FX European-style options (CAD/USD) purchased from a CIRO-regulated dealer for premium-limited hedging
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CAD/USD) documented under an ISDA 2002 with a Schedule I dealer; OSFI margin rules apply only at notional thresholds far above LP scale

NDFs: not applicable to CAD/USD because the Canadian dollar is fully convertible and deliverable under EMTA/ISDA guidelines; NDFs would be permissible solely as back-to-back hedges for non-convertible emerging-market collection currencies and are not recommended for this fitness-app treasury

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 6th month after the LP's fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for calendar-year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: $5/day late-filing penalty up to $100, plus possible gross negligence penalties; CRA may assess partners directly for unpaid taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Slips (T5013IF) to partners and copy to CRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and each limited partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Partner copy by the later of March 31 or 30 days after fiscal period end; CRA copy with the T5013 Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: $25 per slip penalty for late filing/issue, up to $2,500; may trigger additional CRA scrutiny.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (if the LP is registered for GST/HST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Based on reporting period; annual filers due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of the net tax due, plus daily interest; repeated non-filing may lead to mandatory electronic filing and prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Registrar responsible for limited partnerships (e.g., ServiceOntario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the LP's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in forfeiture of the LP's right to sue in the jurisdiction and eventual strike-off/dissolution of the partnership.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for Canadian Limited Partnerships under federal law unless the LP is a reporting issuer or the partnership agreement requires one; provincial variations may impose audit requirements for large partnerships or those with public disclosure requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (for publicly accountable enterprises) or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); financial statements may be prepared on a review engagement or notice-to-reader basis if no audit is required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No federal UBO annual confirmation exists for LPs; the LP must confirm partner allocations and ownership percentages in the T5013 Schedule 5 annually, and any changes in limited partner identities or contributions should be updated in the partnership records. Provincial transparency registries (e.g., British Columbia) may require annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information.
